purpose: Pass/fail criteria for trusting the triage system, fixed BEFORE the first backtest run. Changing this file after registration makes the backtest refuse to run until re-registered (and the re-registration is logged).
unit_of_agreement: System recommendation compared with the fund's real decision: take_call <-> invested, pass <-> passed. A 'hold' is counted as a disagreement for the agreement rate (the system declined to make the case) and is reported separately.
criterion_hit_definition: For each labelled criterion on each memo (data/backtest/memos.json 'expected'): 'high' hits when score >= 6, 'low' hits when score <= 5, 'mid' hits when 4 <= score <= 7.
verdict_rule: TRUST (for advisory use only) if every threshold is met. Otherwise NOT YET: the failing metric names what to fix. Missing data and the candour criterion are excluded from nothing: they are scored as designed.
labelling_rule: Each disagreement gets a one-paragraph judgement citing the memo's reason text. Labelling happens AFTER the run, by a human, and is not used to tune thresholds.
caveats_to_state: n=12 is small: one flip moves agreement by 8 points.
Memo inputs are richer than real applications; the 'what it does' text was written by the fund after meeting the company.
Rubric v0 was drafted from these same memos, so the backtest is in-sample for the rubric. Scoring prompts withhold the memo-derived seed_evidence to limit this.
Research cut-off dates are assumptions (decision dates are not in the pack) and web search cannot be fully date-blocked; outcome-like snippets are flagged and excluded.
Prepnest, and the other uneasy passes, are the interesting disagreements; the fund itself is unsure about them.
